gloss: to see; to come across; to catch sight of

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {目|め}にしていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to see; to come across; to catch sight of
definitions.explanation: To happen to see something or someone, often implying an unplanned or incidental encounter rather than deliberate looking.

examples.japanese: {珍|めずら}しい{光景|こうけい}を{目|め}にした。
examples.english: I came across a rare sight.

examples.japanese: そのニュースを{目|め}にして{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was surprised when I saw that news.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}で{偶然|ぐうぜん}{昔|むかし}の{友人|ゆうじん}を{目|め}にして、{思|おも}わず{声|こえ}をかけた。
examples.english: I happened to spot an old friend in front of the station and called out to them without thinking.

notes:
An idiomatic expression meaning to see or catch sight of something, often implying that the encounter was unplanned or incidental. It carries a slightly more literary or formal tone than {見|み}る.

USAGE:
- Often used when encountering something unexpectedly or for the first time
- Common in written Japanese and news reporting
- Frequently appears in the past tense ({目|め}にした)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {光景|こうけい}を{目|め}にする: to witness a scene
- {記事|きじ}を{目|め}にする: to come across an article
- {現実|げんじつ}を{目|め}にする: to see the reality
- {初|はじ}めて{目|め}にする: to see for the first time

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見|み}る: the basic word for seeing; neutral and general
- {見|み}かける: to happen to see someone; implies spotting a person
- {目撃|もくげき}する: to witness (more dramatic, often used for accidents or crimes)
